title: The Elephant Who Stopped Pulling | Gajendra

lines.text: What do you do when your own strength is not enough?
lines.caps: What do you do when | your own *strength | is *not enough?

lines.text: A huge elephant named Gajendra led his herd to a lake on Mount Trikuta. The day was hot.
He drank, he bathed, he splashed his family. Then a crocodile bit his leg.
lines.caps: He *splashed his family. | Then a *crocodile | bit his leg.

lines.text: He pulled. The crocodile pulled back. His family tried to help, but nobody could free him.
lines.caps: He *pulled. | It pulled *back. | Nobody could *free him.

lines.text: The fight lasted a thousand years in this telling. In the water, the crocodile grew stronger. The elephant grew weak.
lines.caps: A *thousand years. | The crocodile grew *stronger. | He grew *weak.

lines.text: Then Gajendra remembered a prayer from a past life, and stopped pulling.
lines.caps: A *prayer | from a *past life. | He *stopped pulling.

lines.text: He lifted a lotus with his trunk and said: I surrender to the One behind everything.
The gods did not come. He had not called a god. He had called the One behind all gods.
lines.caps: The *gods did not come. | He called the *One | behind all gods.

lines.text: Vishnu arrived on Garuda, so fast that his chakra was still in his hand. He lifted the elephant and the crocodile out of the lake.
lines.caps: Vishnu on *Garuda. | He *lifted them | out of the lake.

lines.text: His chakra freed the elephant. The crocodile became a gandharva named Huhu, released from an old curse.
lines.caps: The *chakra spun. | The crocodile was *Huhu, | freed from a *curse.

lines.text: Gajendra was once a king named Indradyumna, cursed by a sage. He did not win by strength. He won when he let go and called. Follow for more stories.
lines.caps: He did not win by *strength. | He won when he | *called out. | Follow for *more stories.
